We are moving from chatbots that answer questions toward agents that can plan, use tools, write code, interact with systems, and complete tasks. But agents are only one part of what comes next. Here are the technologies I think every developer and student should start watching now.

latest.title: Deploy a Static Website on Amazon S3 + CloudFront
latest.description: In this article, we will learn how to deploy a static website using Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront. Amazon S3 is used to securely store website files such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and images, while CloudFront provides fast and reliable content delivery through AWS edge locations. We will explore how to configure an S3 bucket, connect it to CloudFront using Origin Access Control, enable HTTPS, and understand caching and website updates.

latest.title: Building an AI-Powered Data Quality Assistant on AWS
latest.description: Learn how to build an AI-powered data quality workflow using Amazon S3, AWS Glue, Amazon Athena, and Amazon Bedrock. This project demonstrates how raw datasets can be analyzed for common quality issues such as missing values, duplicate records, inconsistent data, and invalid values, with AI-generated explanations and recommendations for improving data quality.

latest.title: AWS Auto Scaling and Load Balancing: Building Resilient Applications 🚀
latest.description: Learn how Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling and Elastic Load Balancing work together to build scalable and highly available applications on AWS. This article explores load distribution, health checks, scaling policies, fault tolerance, and practical architecture considerations.

trending.title: Build Your First AI Agent on AWS (in about the time it takes to drink a coffee)
trending.description: An LLM answers; an agent acts. In this hands-on walkthrough from a 30-minute meetup talk, I build an AWS Cost Explainer agent live: the whole thing is a model, one tool, and a loop you don't have to write. We use Strands for the agent, Kiro's spec-driven flow to go from plain English to working code, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore as the runtime. Full sample code, a clone-and-run repo, and homework sized to where you are. Come build your first agent.
